messages:
alex: Heads-up — quick sync on multi-format weight ingest strategy. We keep running into edgecases where safetensors + streaming works for hosted but breaks private deploy hotstart. Thoughts on a single ingestion surface vs bifurcated (index-first for private, stream-first for hosted)?

jin: I ran a few failure repros yesterday. Main issues: partial shard checksums, delayed header parsing, and OOM during concurrent warmup. Stream-first is simpler for memory (no big index in memory) but harder to reason for warmstart ordering.

maria: For private deploys we also need verifiable provenance + offline validation (air-gapped). Index-first buys you a fast integrity gate and ability to schedule prioritized warmup. But it creates a large metadata step which increases TTFI (time-to-first-inference) unless we parallelize.

sam: Agree. One pattern: small lightweight manifest (index summary) that fits in memory + per-shard range metadata for streaming. So index-first semantic but still supports byte-range streaming. Minimizes full-index cost.

jin: Prototype manifest I used (very small):
```json
{"format": "mini-manifest.v1", "shards": [{"id":"s0","size":12345678,"ranges":[[0,4096],[4096,8192]],"crc":"abcd1234"}], "activation_order": ["s0","s1"]}
```
Works for warmup prioritization and checksum quick-fail.

alex: Nice. What about safetensors vs tar/zip bundles? do we normalize on safetensors at ingest? safetensors avoids parsing exec payloads but we still need a shim for other formats.

maria: Normalize as a transport concept, not on-disk canonicalization. Support multiple source formats but produce a canonical manifest and an access adapter at ingest time. That adapter exposes a uniform chunk API to the runtime. Keeps runtime simple.

sam: Fallback policy suggestion: if manifest parse succeeds but some shards fail streaming/validation, serve a compatible quantized variant (if we have one) while kicking off a repair job. That keeps app SLAs.

ingest-bot: [ingest-job:job-2026-03-18-09-15] failed to fetch s2 from S3 region-us-west-2 after 3 retries. Marking shard s2 degraded.

jin: That log is exactly the scenario. Our runtime must support degraded shards + graceful quality fallback. Also expose telemetry: percent-shards-validated, warmup-complete, degraded-shards.

alex: Operationally we want two guarantees: 1) quick integrity check (fast-fail bad bundles) 2) predictable warmstart ordering so prefixes hit hot cache. Mini-manifest + streaming adapter seems to hit both.

maria: Also need to decide ABI for adapters: simple methods: open_chunk(shard_id, offset, length) -> stream; get_metadata(shard_id) -> {crc,size,activation_rank}. Keep it language-agnostic (HTTP/gRPC).

sam: One more: eviction/warmup interplay. If we do activation_order, eviction must prefer later-activation shards first. Otherwise we thrash. Add per-shard activation_rank -> eviction_score.

alex: TL;DR proposal in-thread: micro-manifest (index summary) + streaming chunk adapter + adapter ABI + fallback-to-quantized-variant + telemetry signals. Next steps: put this in an RFC, small PoC proto (jin + sam) and ops checklist for private deploys (maria). :thumbsup:

maria: I'll draft ops checklist: validation-in-airgap, KMS signing for manifests, repair-runbook.

jin: I'll push a PoC server that serves the mini-manifest and a byte-range stream adapter by EOW.

sam: I'll sketch eviction policy changes and a simulation to show warmup hit-rate improvement.

alex: Cool — schedule a 30m follow-up after PoC. Thanks everyone.
